Kings county to enforce vehicle weight restriction on such interstate by means
of mobile or stationary weigh in motion systems; and providing for the repeal
of such provisions upon expiration thereof

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2740

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers law,
in relation to establishing a demonstration program on interstate route
278 in Kings county to enforce vehicle weight restriction on such inter-
state by means of mobile or stationary weigh in motion systems; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To create a weigh-in-motion pilot program for the enforcement of vehicle
weight restrictions on the portion of Interstate 278 located in Brook-
lyn.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill adds a new Section 385-a to the Vehicle and
Traffic Law, which authorizes the City of New York to create a pilot
weigh-in-motion enforcement program for the Brooklyn Queens Expressway
in Brooklyn. The program shall impose fines for failure to comply with
existing weight restrictions. The New York State Department of Transpor-
tation will enter into an MOU with the New York City Department of
Transportation for the purposes of carrying out the program, including
the installation of up to thirty weigh-in-motion systems along Inter-
state 278 in Brooklyn. Section one also establishes the parameters of
the pilot program, including privacy protections and restrictions on the
retention of data and images of affected individuals and vehicles, the
maintenance of the system, the fines imposed, the scope of infractions,
the manner of notification of infractions, adjudication of liability,
and an annual process to report the results of the program.

Section two of the bill amends Section 237 of the Vehicle and Traffic
Law to allow the adjudication of liability for any violation found
pursuant to the program by the New York City Parking Violations Bureau.

Section three of the bill amends Subdivision 2 of Section 87 of the
Public Officers Law by adding any recorded materials collected pursuant
to the program to a list of exceptions to the otherwise applicable
public disclosure law.

Section four of the bill outlines that the City Department of Transpor-
tation shall create proper awareness among the public of the new
program, shall issue a warning rather than a violation for the first 90
days of the program, and shall promulgate any and all rules and regu-
lations required to implement the program.

Section five of the bill sets forth the effective date and the date of
expiration.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The respective final reports of the New York City Mayor's Expert Panel
and the New York City Council on the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway,
released in early 2020, found that this vital piece of infrastructure is
in dire condition. The Panel's report focused on the 1.5-mile stretch of
the roadway from Sands Street to Atlantic Avenue-which includes the
"triple cantilever" structure running along the edge of Brooklyn Heights
with a northbound level, southbound level, and the Brooklyn Heights
promenade-and found the structure to be deteriorating rapidly, with
sections possibly unsafe for vehicular and truck traffic in five years
if mitigations are not made expeditiously.

One reason for the expressway's crumbling infrastructure is the presence
of overweight truck traffic. There is currently minimal enforcement of
truck weight restriction, in part because the conventional enforcement
method of taking a truck off the road and weighing it on a stationary
scale is highly impractical on a highway as congested and narrow as the
BQE. This legislation would allow for the City of New York, in conjunc-
tion with the State, to institute a weigh-in-motion system on the 1-278
in Brooklyn that would increase enforcement of weight restrictions.
Weigh-in-motion systems record the axle.weights and gross weights of
vehicles that drive over the site of the system, without the need for
the vehicles to stop. This bill would create an enforcement program that
would automatically issue violations for trucks that are recorded as
having weights substantially above the existing legal limits.

By significantly reducing overweight truck traffic on the BQE, this
legislation will serve as an important step to protect this critical
component of the network of roadways that enable passenger and freight
vehicles to flow throughout the New York area. The enforcement program,
coupled with an emergency repair initiative the City Department of
Transportation will undertake, will extend the life of the existing
structure until long-term approaches to the 1-278 corridor can be imple-
mented.

 
LEGISLATIVE. HISTORY:

2020:S8128A (Kavanagh) - TRANSPORTATION

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
(a) This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and be
deemed repealed three years after the first notice of liability issued
for violations recorded by weigh in motion systems.
(b) Notwithstanding the expiration and repeal of this act, any notices
of liability issued pursuant to section three hundred eighty-five-a of
the vehicle and traffic law, as added by section one of this act, prior
to the expiration date of this act may be adjudicated after such expira-
tion date.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2740B            Revised 6/3/2021

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers law,
in relation to establishing a demonstration program on interstate route
278 in Kings county to enforce vehicle weight restriction on such inter-
state by means of mobile or stationary weigh in motion systems; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To create a weigh-in-motion pilot program for the enforcement of vehicle
weight restrictions on the portion of Interstate 278 located in Brook-
lyn.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections one through six of the bill would repeal and re-enact various
provisions of VTL Article 2-B pertaining to localities' administrative
tribunal adjudications of liability for violations arising from existing
demonstration programs (and incorporating the newly authorized BQE
demonstration program) involving traffic related photo violation-moni-
toring systems. Subdivision (3) of the new VTL § 235 would make clear
that the repeal and reenactment of provisions of Article 2-B are not
intended to confer new jurisdiction upon localities with respect to the
matters specified in such subdivision.

Section seven of the bill repeals paragraph a of subdivision 5-a of
section 401 of the vehicle and traffic law and adds a new paragraph a in
its place relating to penalties arising from such camera programs that
have not been satisfied at the time of vehicle registration.

Sections eight through ten of the bill amend and repeal portions of
section 1809 of the vehicle and traffic law relating to monetary
surcharges imposed in connection with traffic related photo violation-
monitoring systems.

Section eleven of the bill amends the general municipal law by adding a
new section 371-a to address photo violation-monitoring demonstration
programs that are adjudicated by Traffic Violations Agencies in Nassau
and Suffolk Counties, Buffalo and Rochester.

Section twelve of the bill amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding
a new section 385-a authorizing the City of New York to establish a
demonstration weigh in motion system program on interstate route 278 in
Brooklyn (also known as the Brooklyn Queens Expressway or "BQE"),
specifically from the vicinity of Atlantic Avenue to the vicinity of
Sands Street, for the enforcement of vehicle weight and/or axle weight
restrictions. This would allow the New York City Department of Transpor-
tation to install and operate up to sixteen weigh in motion systems on
this portion of the BQE and impose monetary penalties on owners of vehi-
cles for failure of such vehicles to comply with vehicle weight and/or
axle weight restrictions. NYC DOT would be authorized to enter into an
agreement with the New York State Department of Transportation for
purposes of coordinating the planning, design, installation,
construction and maintenance of the pilot program system. The bill
addresses the extensive measures that would be taken to protect drivers'
privacy and safeguard the data obtained from implementation of the
program. Moreover, it would require that technicians review the eviden-
tiary materials produced by the weigh in motion system for each
violation and sign a certificate swearing to or affirming their accura-
cy, but consistent with existing procedures relating to similar adminis-
trative violations, it is not intended that these certificates be nota-
rized. The City's Parking Violations Bureau would adjudicate the notices
of liability issued in connection with this demonstration program.

Section thirteen amends subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public offi-
cers law by adding a new paragraph r to exempt from public access the
photographic and other information and data generated by this program.

Section fourteen of the bill directs the New York City Department of
Transportation to communicate with the public about the program prior to
its implementation, and provides a grace period during the initial 90
days of the program whereby written warnings, instead of notices of
violation, shall be sent to drivers.

Section fifteen of the bill subjects purchases or leases of necessary
equipment for the program to section 103 of the general municipal law.

Section sixteen of the bill sets forth the effective date, providing
that the law would take effect immediately (with the proposed demon-
stration program expiring on December 1, 2025); and addresses the vari-
ous expiration dates set forth in the amendments to VTL § 1809 made by
sections 8 and 8-a through 8-g regarding mandatory surcharges in
connection with various camera demonstration programs.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2019, New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio convened a panel of experts
to review the City's planned reconstruction of the BQE from Atlantic
Avenue to Sands Street in Brooklyn. The findings of their report lead to
the undisputable conclusion that this corridor along the BQE is in
urgent need of repair, and that illegally overweight trucks were
contributing significantly to the structure's deterioration.

Higher live loads from overweight trucks cause greater stress on the
structure, shorten its lifespan, decrease reliability, and reduce safe-
ty. Although the structure has an 80,000-pound limit for trucks, data
collected at the request of the Panel between October 16, 2019 and Janu-
ary 19, 2020 showed that on the Queens-bound roadway, 11.1 percent of
trucks exceeded 80,000 pounds and 27 percent exceeded the Federal Bridge
Formula, which limits the weight-to-length ratio of vehicles crossing a
bridge.

Following the Panel's findings and recommendations, Mayor de Blasio
directed the New York City Police Department to conduct in-person
enforcement on this corridor, and NYCDOT has continued to employ struc-
tural monitoring and overweight vehicle monitoring. Although NYCDOT has
seen some reduction in overweight vehicles on this corridor since this
enforcement began, it requires ongoing NYPD personnel presence. This can
be challenging to sustain on a permanent ongoing basis, and the config-
uration of this segment of the BQE makes pulling over trucks and weigh-
ing them logistically challenging.


This bill would authorize automated enforcement on this portion of the
BQE, and would enable expanded enforcement efforts and hours.  Enforce-
ment would utilize weigh in motion systems paired with cameras, similar
to New York City's successful automated school speed zone and red light
camera programs. Violations would carry the same or a lower penalty than
the often-hefty penalties issued by police officers during in-person
enforcement; and only trucks overweight by at least 10 percent would be
issued a fine.

The overall goal of the amendments proposed in sections 1 through 11 is
to consolidate, in an orderly and integrated legislative scheme, the
underlying implementation provisions of these existing (and newly
proposed) photo violation-monitoring demonstration programs that have
been enacted over the last several years. The bill would accomplish this
with respect to the forum for such adjudications within Article 2-B, as
well as provisions of the vehicle and traffic law (VTL) related to such
programs involving vehicle registration and mandatory surcharges. Going
forward, the provisions of the VTL that have established these demon-
stration programs would continue to identify their duration (i.e.,
effective dates and related expiration sections), but the sections that
would be added or amended by this law would not be subject to the
complex and confusing reverter provisions that have heretofore existed.

For the foregoing reasons, this bill will be an important step towards
preserving a critical roadway in a heavily trafficked corridor through a
measure implemented by proven technologies and enforcement efforts.
These camera enforcement pilot programs have shown over time to be inno-
vative and effective tools for counties and other localities to address
and implement safety measures on their public roadways. The recodifica-
tion of the applicable VTL provisions will result in a more comprehen-
sive and comprehensible operationalization of such programs.

 
LEGISLATIVE. HISTORY:

2020: S8128A (Kavanagh) / A10223 (Simon) - TRANSPORTATION

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that sections
twelve, thirteen, fourteen and fifteen shall expire and be deemed
repealed December 1, 2025 when upon such date the provisions of such
sections shall be deemed repealed; and provided further, that notwith-
standing the expiration and repeal of sections twelve, thirteen, four-
teen and fifteen of this act, any notices of liability issued pursuant
to the demonstration program authorized pursuant to section 385-a of the
vehicle and traffic law, as added by section twelve of this act, prior
to the expiration date of this act may be adjudicated after such expira-
tion date; and provided further, that:
(a) the amendments to the opening paragraph and paragraph (c) of subdi-
vision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and traffic law made by section
eight of this act shall not affect the expiration of such section and
shall be deemed to expire therewith, when upon such date the provisions
of section eight-a of this act shall take effect;
(b) the amendments to the opening paragraph and paragraph (c) of subdi-
vision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and traffic law made by section
eight-a of this act shall not affect the expiration of such section and
shall be deemed to expire therewith, when upon such date the provisions
of section eight-b of this act shall take effect;
(c) the amendments to subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and
traffic law made by section eight-b of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith, when
upon such date the provisions of section eight-c of this act shall take
effect;
(d) the amendments to subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and
traffic law made by section eight-c of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith, when
upon such date the provisions of section eight-d of this act shall take
effect;
(e) the amendments to subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and
traffic law made by section eight-d of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith, when
upon such date the provisions of section eight-e of this act shall take
effect;
(f) the amendments to subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and
traffic law made by section eight-e of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith, when
upon such date the provisions of section eight-f of this act shall take
effect;
(g) the amendments to subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and
traffic law made by section eight-f of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith, when
upon such date the provisions of section eight-g of this act shall take
effect; and
(h) the amendments to subdivision 1 of section 1809 of the vehicle and
traffic law made by section eight-g of this act shall not affect the
expiration of such section and shall be deemed to expire therewith, when
upon such date the provisions of section eight-h of this act shall take
effect.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 151 Chapter 773
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2740-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers
        law,  in  relation  to  establishing  a demonstration program on
        interstate route 278 in Kings county to enforce  vehicle  weight
        restriction  on such interstate by means of mobile or stationary
        weigh in motion systems; and providing for the  repeal  of  such
        provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  authorizes automated enforcement of vehicle weight limita-
tions on the triple cantilever portion of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway
(BQE), a critical roadway in New York City's transportation system.

  Enforcement of weight limits for vehicles traveling on the roadway  is
essential in light of the need for roadway rehabilitation.
 
  This  bill  allows  for  installation  of a "weigh in motion violation
monitoring system," which involves sensors to detect the weight of vehi-
cles, automating the process to ensure  more  consistent  and  efficient
enforcement  of  weight  restrictions. It will also relieve the New York
Police Department from having to enforce weight  restrictions  manually,
and  would set forth uniform penalties and a process for adjudication of
violations.
 
  This bill is an innovative, common-sense approach to address the needs
of our vital infrastructure.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to establishing a demonstration program on interstate route 278 in Kings county to enforce vehicle weight restriction on such interstate by means of mobile or stationary weigh in motion systems; relates to notices of liability and the adjudication of certain traffic infractions involving the use of photo monitoring devices.
